observations:
Torah #119 is a micro-teaching with only 1 bechina edge in the dataset ({שבת, דעת}) and a source text of 7 lines. No independent bechina domain of 3+ concepts was found that is structurally separate from the existing package.

The two gap concepts proposed in torah_119_additions.json (כַּעַס and כְּסִילוּת) form a bechina pair and could theoretically constitute a new evil-polarity package. However, they do not meet the threshold for a new package because:
1. They form only a 2-node component (insufficient for an independent package — the framework notes small 1-2 node components should be merged into closest existing package).
2. They are explicitly positioned as the evil mirror within the SAME teaching's binary axis: Shabbat/daas/compassion vs. weekday-folly/anger/no-compassion. The evil pole is not structurally separate — it is the negation of the single package's dominant concept (דַּעַת). Anger = absence of daas = absence of Shabbat-quality. This makes כַּעַס/כְּסִילוּת belong in Package 1 as the evil members of the same conceptual axis, not as a separate package.
3. The good/evil mirror structure here is unusually simple: there is only one axis in the entire Torah. Torah #119 does not have separate thematic domains with independent evil counterparts (unlike Torah #1 which has multiple packages each with their own evil mirror). The single axis is: Shabbat-daas-compassion (good) vs. weekday-folly-anger (evil). Both poles belong in Package 1.

The Torah's argument follows a two-stage structure:
  Stage 1 — Conceptual equation [Package 1: good bechina core]
    שַׁבָּת = דַּעַת (Shabbat is the temporal manifestation of divine knowledge)
  Stage 2 — Eitza chain flowing from Package 1
    דַּעַת → רַחֲמָנוּת → שֶׁיִּהְיֶה לוֹ רַחֲמִים עַל אֲחֵרִים → מְרַחֲמִין עָלָיו
    (daas → capacity for compassion → acts of compassion → receiving divine compassion)

The evil mirror is entirely contained within the single package: כְּסִילוּת (absence of daas = weekday folly) produces כַּעַס (anger = absence of compassion). These are the evil poles of the same axis, not a separate thematic domain.

Conclusion: Torah #119 is a single-package Torah. Its conceptual structure is a single binary axis with a good pole (Shabbat/daas) and an evil pole (folly/anger), plus a practical eitza chain that derives from the good pole. No new packages are warranted.
